Gotta give it Claude as a vacation planner. Less than two weeks ago I figured out some time off was a necessity. Gave me several options and it worked out so well. It even made fun of the books I tried to pack, calling them my job wearing a snorkel.
Vacay fun: tried to pick out a movie to watch together. 16 yo son said Obsession, I said Anaconda, and hubby was appalled at all the hotel options. Went out for ice cream at Chaps instead.
Today’s reflection: an intellectual commitment to principles doesn’t mean you live them fully. Also, octagon rooms are lovely. #Monticello

I was musing over the weekend about where EJMR would go now that the site's been shut down. I hadn't expected The Economist to be the answer.

So what’s a better place for info? I used to point students to #EconTwitter, but the algo there is awful, amplifying pile-ons over convos, and Elon drove many off the platform. Bluesky doesn't quite feel like it has critical mass yet, but it might be closer.

Economics Job Market Rumors started back when I was on the job market 20 years ago. I remember how much the uncertainty of getting a job makes you seek out any kind of info. But quality matters. An anon forum was never going to cut it. And it would breed bad behavior. It did.

I heard this week that the cesspool econ website EJMR went dark. it’s been offline for over a week now. no tears shed here. solid poetic justice that unrelenting AI bot attacks appear to have been its downfall. but it raises a question: where does the demand for info go next?
